thread:
olivia: quick heads-up — ran a playback run against the 'edge' cohort and saw intermittent latency spikes tied to kernel fallback. attaching initial logs.

sam: can you paste the sample slice or trace id? want to see the exact op that triggered fallback.

olivia: cohort=A1-edge-031, trace=0x7af3b9. snippet below:
```
[2026-01-14T12:45:02Z] kernel_selector: choose matmul_opt_v2
[2026-01-14T12:45:02Z] kernel_selector: fallback to matmul_generic (reason: estimated_temp_bytes 1.8GB > threshold 1.6GB)
[2026-01-14T12:45:02Z] kvcache: miss seq=427 warmup=0
[2026-01-14T12:45:02Z] latency: request 12.4ms -> 88.7ms spike
```

mike: fallback shouldn't happen in a strict apples-to-apples playback unless kernel cache or selector config changed. Did you pin the kernel catalog & selector version for this run?

olivia: I pinned model hash and runtime tag but not the kernel catalog. this was a nightly run (kernels from 2026-01-14-nightly).

raj: another vector: playback compresses inter-arrival times slightly; the continuous-batching merge could create larger temporary buffers for some batched ops — bumping estimated_temp_bytes for merged batches might flip selector choice.

sam: confirm: playback honors original request boundaries, but the harness' timing sampler can shrink long gaps into shorter ones (we have a 'time-delta-clamp' to avoid extreme gaps). could be causing more merging.

tanya: I can re-run with two knobs: (A) kernel catalog pinned, (B) IA-time clamp set to preserve original spacing exactly. which do you want first?

olivia: both. run A then A+B. kicked off job 8792.

ci-bot: build 2026-01-14-nightly kernels deployed to test pool k8s-runtimeset-7

(1h)

olivia: job 8792 done. results summarized:
- run A (pinned-kernels): spike persisted (same kernel choices as nightly)  
- run A+B (pinned-kernels + no-merge timing): spike disappeared  
KV hitrate ~ identical across runs (~82%).
attached: quick flame graph excerpt and selector trace.

sam: interesting. if KV hitrate didn't change but spikes vanish when merging is prevented then merging must be pushing a per-op temp buffer peak over the selector threshold, causing fallback to a slower generic kernel.

mike: that's consistent with selector logic — it estimates temporary workspace per-op using batch shape * peak activations. merged requests can increase transient peak beyond the per-request sum because op scheduling changes.

raj: concrete hypothesis: merged batches increase the peak temporary buffer at a specific op (matmul) causing fallback. solution options:
- option1: increase buffer-budget-threshold for merged path so selector keeps fast kernels
- option2: limit merge shapes (cap max batch dims) to avoid crossing the threshold
- option3: teach selector to account for kvcache prefix sizes and merged IA patterns when estimating temp bytes

tanya: I can prototype option2 quickly in the harness (cap merged batch seq_len*batchdim). mike, can you add selector logging of estimated_temp_bytes into the playback traces? that will help validate.

mike: on it. PR to add selector_est_temp_bytes field to trace logs and a harness mode to forbid merging is up: https://git.redwood/infr/mx/PR-4822

olivia: ran the no-merge variant again with selector logging. here is the critical line from the selector trace:
```
selector_est_temp_bytes: merged_run=1.82GB, no_merge=1.45GB, threshold=1.6GB
selected_kernel: merged_run -> matmul_generic ; no_merge -> matmul_opt_v2
```

sam: that matches exactly. mitigation path: quick fix is option2 (cap merging), medium-term: improve selector heuristics and expose a per-cfg merged-budget param.

mike: I'll prototype the cap and add a runtime flag. also adding an assert in the harness to fail-if-kernel-change when apples-to-apples mode enabled.

tanya: we'll also add a note in the harness README about 'deterministic-kernel' mode so SRE/bench teams can run apples-to-apples without kernel churn.

olivia: filing INF-7234 with artifacts and links to job 8792 + PR-4822. tagging for eng-runtime + eng-sre.

sam: thanks — when INF-7234 exists ping here and we can triage priority. :thumbsup:

olivia: INF-7234 created: https://jira.redwood/INF-7234 — moving follow-ups there. closing thread.
